Genomic relationship matrix from genotype data

Source: R/genomic_relationship.R
genomic_relationship.Rd

Computes the VanRaden (2008) genomic relationship matrix (GRM) from biallelic marker genotypes, for use as the A argument of lmm_animal.

Usage

genomic_relationship(M, p = NULL, maf = 0.01, max_missing = 0.1, blend = 0)

Arguments

M

Numeric genotype matrix with individuals in rows and markers in columns, coded as the number of copies (0, 1, 2) of the counted allele. Missing genotypes are allowed (NA); non-integer values such as imputed dosages are also accepted.

p

Optional vector of allele frequencies of the counted allele, one per column of M. If NULL (default), they are estimated from M as colMeans(M, na.rm = TRUE) / 2. Supplying base-population frequencies is recommended when they are known.

maf

Markers with minor allele frequency below this value are dropped. Monomorphic markers (and, when p is estimated, markers with a single observed genotype class) are always dropped.

max_missing

Markers with a proportion of missing genotypes above this value are dropped. Fully missing markers are always dropped, even when max_missing = 1 and p is supplied.

blend

Weight w in (1 - w) * G + w * I. Default 0 returns the raw GRM; a small value (e.g. 0.01) makes a singular GRM, such as one with fewer markers than individuals or duplicated genotypes, positive definite.

Value

A symmetric positive-semidefinite matrix with the individuals' row names of M on both dimensions. The number of markers used and their scaling constant are stored in the attributes n_markers and scale.

Details

The GRM is G = Z %*% t(Z) / (2 * sum(p * (1 - p))), where Z = M - 2p. Missing genotypes are replaced by their expected value 2p, so they contribute zero to the numerator. Fully missing markers are excluded from both numerator and denominator; if other markers remain, a warning is issued when they would otherwise pass the filters. With frequencies estimated from the data, the diagonal averages about one plus the inbreeding coefficient, and the off-diagonals are relative to the sample average.

References

VanRaden, P.M. (2008). Efficient methods to compute genomic predictions. Journal of Dairy Science 91: 4414-4423.

Examples

set.seed(1)
M <- matrix(rbinom(50 * 500, 2, 0.3), nrow = 50)
G <- genomic_relationship(M, blend = 0.01)
dim(G)
#> [1] 50 50
